vocabulary.definition: The process of making a planet or similar environment habitable for life, typically by altering its atmosphere, temperature, or ecology.
vocabulary.example: Scientists are researching terraforming techniques to potentially make Mars suitable for human colonization.

vocabulary.definition: The process of growth or increase, typically by gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter.
vocabulary.example: The accretion of dust and gas around a forming star contributes to the creation of planets.

vocabulary.definition: A measure of the amount of rotation an object has, taking into account its mass and its speed of rotation.
vocabulary.example: The conservation of angular momentum explains why a figure skater spins faster when pulling in their arms.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to achieve a desired result with minimal wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.example: The new manufacturing process significantly improved efficiency and reduced production costs.

vocabulary.definition: Very small pieces or bits; fragments.
vocabulary.example: The explosion shattered the vase into smithereens, making it impossible to repair.

vocabulary.definition: A large group of people or things; often used to indicate a vast number or quantity.
vocabulary.example: The company hired a legion of temporary workers to handle the increased demand during the holiday season.
